name: 3.5mm TRS (stereo audio jack)
ascii:
sleeve         ring          tip
        |             |             |
   =====+=============+=============+===>   (insert ->)
        |             |             |
        S             R             T
       GND          Right     Left / signal
description: The 3.5mm phone jack. Conductors from the tip inward: Tip, Ring, Sleeve. In stereo audio Tip = Left, Ring = Right, Sleeve = ground. A 2-conductor TS plug (no ring) is mono: Tip = signal, Sleeve = ground -- this is the plug Eurorack uses for CV and audio patch cables. A 4-conductor TRRS adds a second ring for a microphone.

contacts.name: Tip
contacts.description: left channel (stereo TRS) or the single signal (mono TS); the hot / balanced + on a balanced TRS

contacts.name: Ring
contacts.description: right channel (stereo TRS) or cold / balanced - (balanced mono); absent on a mono TS plug

variants: TS (2-conductor, Tip + Sleeve): mono, Tip = signal, Sleeve = ground. This is the Eurorack patch cable -- CV and audio are unbalanced mono.
TRS (3-conductor, this): stereo (Tip=L, Ring=R, Sleeve=GND) OR balanced mono (Tip=+, Ring=-, Sleeve=GND). Context decides which.
TRRS (4-conductor): adds a microphone conductor. Two incompatible standards: CTIA (common: T=L, R=R, R2=GND, S=MIC) and OMTP (older: R2=MIC, S=GND). Plugging one into the other swaps mic and ground.
gotchas: Eurorack uses mono TS 3.5mm, not TRS -- CV and audio are unbalanced. A stereo TRS cable in a Eurorack jack shorts the ring, usually harmless but not what you want.
Balanced TRS and stereo TRS are physically identical; only the wiring intent differs. A balanced mono signal into a stereo input plays only on the left, and vice versa.
TRRS mic order (CTIA vs OMTP) is the classic 'my headset mic doesn't work' trap -- a $2 CTIA/OMTP adapter swaps the last two conductors.
Sleeve makes contact first and breaks last on insert/remove, so unplugging a live jack thumps the ground before the signal (the loud pop you hear).
notes: 3.5mm TRS conductor assignment (Tip=L, Ring=R, Sleeve=GND) is the universal stereo convention; TS/TRRS variants noted. Eurorack TS-mono usage called out for the user's synth work.
